    mutate(across(everything(), ~ . / sum(.)))

# PERMANOVA for controls

adonis2(formula = dm.asv_control ~ sample_type, data = metadata_table_control_df, permutations = 999)

For now, let's just make a heatmap here that will showcase this the easiest at a genera-level.

genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df = genera_rollup_experiment_df %>%
  rownames_to_column(var="genera_id")

#There's a whole bunch of genera here that are super low abundance. So lets just make this cleaner by plotting only those genera that have more than 0.5% of total abundance. Random cutoff.

# Step 1: Calculate the total abundance for each genus
genera_totals <- rowSums(genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df[, -1])

# Step 2: Calculate the threshold for 0.5% of the overall population
total_abundance <- sum(genera_totals)
threshold <- total_abundance * 0.005

# Step 3: Separate the genera that are above the threshold and those that are below it
above_threshold <- genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df[genera_totals >= threshold, ]
below_threshold <- genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df[genera_totals < threshold, ]

# Step 4: Sum the abundance of the below-threshold genera by column
below_threshold_sum <- colSums(below_threshold[, -1])

# Step 5: Create a new row for the aggregated below-threshold genera
new_row <- data.frame(genera_id = "under 0.5% of abundance", t(below_threshold_sum))
colnames(new_row) <- colnames(genera_rollup_experiment_heatmap_df)

above_threshold <- as.data.frame(above_threshold)
new_row <- as.data.frame(new_row)

#Super loosey-goosey here. Let's just run an nmds. I know the stress is off. And i know i need to further filter. But just to show Kitt.

# Function to perform metaMDS per site
run_metaMDS <- function(df, metadata, site_column) {
  sites <- unique(metadata[[site_column]])
  nmds_list <- list()
  
  for (site in sites) {
    # Filter ASV table and metadata for the current site
    site_asv <- df[, metadata[[site_column]] == site, drop = FALSE]
    site_metadata <- metadata[metadata[[site_column]] == site, ]
    
    # Ensure there are columns/rows to process
    if (ncol(site_asv) > 1 && nrow(site_metadata) > 1) {
      # Calculate NMDS
      nmds_result <- metaMDS(t(site_asv), distance = "bray", noshare = TRUE, trace = 1, autotransform = TRUE)
      
      # Extract scores and add metadata
      scores_df <- as.data.frame(scores(nmds_result)$sites)
      scores_df$sample_type = site_metadata$sample_type
      scores_df$SampleID = rownames(scores_df)
      scores_df$sample_point = site_metadata$sample_point
      scores_df$site = site
      
      # Append to list
      nmds_list[[site]] <- scores_df
    }
  }
  
  # Combine all NMDS results into one data frame
  combined_nmds_df <- do.call(rbind, nmds_list)
  
  return(combined_nmds_df)
}

#Here we go. I think there is a significant trend here for 46001. Run the stats:

# Function to perform adonis2 per site
run_adonis2_per_site <- function(df, metadata, site_column, sample_type_column) {
  sites <- unique(metadata[[site_column]])
  adonis2_results <- list()
  
  for (site in sites) {
    # Filter ASV table and metadata for the current site
    site_asv <- df[, metadata[[site_column]] == site, drop = FALSE]
    site_metadata <- metadata[metadata[[site_column]] == site, ]
    
    # Ensure there are columns/rows to process
    if (ncol(site_asv) > 1 && nrow(site_metadata) > 1) {
      # Calculate Bray-Curtis distance matrix
      dm <- vegdist(t(site_asv), method = "bray")
      
      # Run adonis2
      adonis2_result <- adonis2(formula = dm ~ sample_type, data = site_metadata, permutations = 999)
      
      # Store result
      adonis2_results[[site]] <- adonis2_result
    }
  }
  
  return(adonis2_results)
}


# Run adonis2 for each site, testing the effect of sample_type
adonis2_results <- run_adonis2_per_site(asv_table_experiment_df_SITES_FINAL_rel, metadata_table_experiment_df_SITES_FINAL, "site", "sample_type")

# Print results
for (site in names(adonis2_results)) {
  cat("\nAdonis2 results for site:", site, "\n")
  print(adonis2_results[[site]])
}

#Nothing really significant here after i subset this data for the handful of sites that we did have data for to compare. Up to this point, the ASV communities (and genera) are significantly different across sites, but not across sample types. I.e., the biology does not seem to be affected by the coal combustion plants. Now, I'm going to see if i can piece out anything on the chemistry side of things below.

#Now let's do some PERMANOVA's and some NMDS to see if chemistry are unique across these different conditions.

#Making a metadata table from the chemistry df itself:
chemistry_metadat = chemistry_df_final %>%
  select(c(1:4))

#Now lets organize the chem table
chemistry_df_withNA_input = chemistry_df_final %>%
  column_to_rownames(var="site_id") %>%
  select(-c(1:3)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) #make numeric because it'll yell if not below.

#Ho boy. Lot of chemistry that is missing values here. Going to have to chop some of these off. Also - there are a significant amount of negative numbers in this dataset. There is no such thing as negative measurement here. Lets make everything that is less than 0 just a 0.

chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop = chemistry_df_withNA_input %>%
  select(-c(alk_bicarb, alk_carb, alk_total, Cl, Cu, DO, Mn, Ni, Mg, ORP, ph_lab, TURB, Zn)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(. < 0, 0, .)))
  
# PERMANOVA for controls
dm.chem_control=calc_dm(t(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop), method = "bray")
adonis2(formula = dm.chem_control ~ Sample.Type, data = chemistry_metadat, permutations = 999)
adonis2(formula = dm.chem_control ~ Site, data = chemistry_metadat, permutations = 999)
adonis2(formula = dm.chem_control ~ Sample.Type + Site, data = chemistry_metadat, permutations = 999)

#Looks like Sample Type and Site are both significantly different here. Let's do some pairwise comparisons.

chemical_data_formerge <- as.data.frame(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop)

# Ensure metadata rows match the sample IDs in chemical_data
metadata <- chemistry_metadat[chemistry_metadat$site_id %in% rownames(chemical_data_formerge), ]

# Add Sample IDs as a column
chemical_data_formerge$site_id <- rownames(chemical_data_formerge)

# Merge chemical data with metadata
chem_merged <- chemical_data_formerge %>%
  inner_join(metadata, by = 'site_id') %>%
  select(-c(Sample.Point))

# Automatically identify chemical columns (excluding metadata columns)
metadata_columns <- c('site_id', 'Sample.Type', 'Site') # Add any other columns that are not chemical measurements
chemical_columns <- setdiff(colnames(chem_merged), metadata_columns)

# Run ANOVA for each chemical value and perform TukeyHSD post-hoc test
anova_results <- list()
tukey_results <- list()
significant_anovas <- list()
significant_tukeys <- list()

for (chemical_col in chemical_columns) {
  anova_result <- aov(as.formula(paste(chemical_col, "~ Sample.Type")), data = chem_merged)
  anova_summary <- summary(anova_result)
  anova_results[[chemical_col]] <- anova_summary
  
  # Check if the ANOVA is significant (p-value < 0.05)
  if (anova_summary[[1]]$`Pr(>F)`[1] < 0.05) {
    significant_anovas[[chemical_col]] <- anova_summary
    
    # Post-hoc Tukey test
    tukey_result <- TukeyHSD(anova_result, "Sample.Type")
    
    # Filter significant results from TukeyHSD
    if (any(tukey_result$`Sample.Type`[, "p adj"] < 0.05)) {
      significant_tukeys[[chemical_col]] <- tukey_result
    }
  }
}


# Print significant TukeyHSD test results for pairwise comparison in significant ANOVAs
cat("\nSignificant TukeyHSD results:\n")
print(significant_tukeys)

#

chem_merge_SITES = chem_merged %>%
  filter(!grepl("13116", Site)) %>%
  filter(!grepl("25410", Site)) %>%
  filter(!grepl("25427", Site)) %>%
  filter(!grepl("42195", Site)) %>%
  filter(!grepl("42201", Site)) %>%
  filter(!grepl("35406", Site))


# Assuming chem_merge_SITES is your dataframe
chem_merge_SITES$Sample.Type <- as.factor(chem_merge_SITES$Sample.Type)
chem_merge_SITES$Site <- as.factor(chem_merge_SITES$Site)

# Exclude non-numeric columns for pivoting
numeric_columns <- setdiff(names(chem_merge_SITES), c("Site", "Sample.Type", "site_id"))

chem_long <- chem_merge_SITES %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = all_of(numeric_columns), names_to = "Chemistry", values_to = "Value")

anova_results <- chem_long %>%
    group_by(Site, Chemistry) %>%
    do(tidy(aov(Value ~ Sample.Type, data = .)))

# Filter for significant results (p-value < 0.05)
significant_anova <- anova_results %>%
    filter(p.value < 0.05 & term == "Sample.Type")

posthoc_results <- chem_long %>%
    filter(Chemistry %in% significant_anova$Chemistry & Site %in% significant_anova$Site) %>%
    group_by(Site, Chemistry) %>%
    do(tidy(TukeyHSD(aov(Value ~ Sample.Type, data = .))))

significant_posthoc <- posthoc_results %>%
    filter(adj.p.value < 0.05)

print(significant_posthoc)

# Extract significant pair-wise comparisons specifically for GW-Upgradient-GW-Downgradient
significant_posthoc <- posthoc_results %>%
    filter(adj.p.value < 0.05 & str_detect(contrast, "GW-Upgradient-GW-Downgradient"))

# Summarize the number of significant p-values per site
significant_summary <- significant_posthoc %>%
    group_by(Site) %>%
    summarize(count = n())

# Plot the number of significant p-values for each site
ggplot(significant_summary, aes(x = reorder(Site, -count), y = count)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    labs(title = "Number of Significant P-Values for GW-Upgradient vs. GW-Downgradient by Site",
         x = "Site", y = "Number of Significant P-Values") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

#It looks like the only Site that has significantly different values between GW-Upgradient and GW-Downgradient is: 46001 and that is for F, Ba, and Temp. However, take with caution because this site only has 2 samples in GW-Upgradient and 3 in GW-Downgradient.

# Extract significant pair-wise comparisons
significant_posthoc <- posthoc_results %>%
    filter(adj.p.value < 0.05)

# Summarize the number of significant p-values per site and contrast
significant_summary <- significant_posthoc %>%
    group_by(Site, contrast) %>%
    summarize(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')

# Filter out sites with no significant p-values
significant_sites <- significant_summary %>%
    group_by(Site) %>%
    filter(sum(count) > 0) %>%
    ungroup()

# Function to plot significant p-values for each site
significant_chemdiffs_plots = ggplot(significant_sites, aes(x = contrast, y = count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ Site, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Faceted Bar Plot by Site",
       x = "Contrast",
       y = "Count") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

#start with prcomp
chem.pca_log<-prcomp(na.omit(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop), center=TRUE, scale.=TRUE)

scores(fit_ord, "vectors")

plot(chemord)

chem.variables_log<-predict(chem.pca_log)

#This establishes the coordinates for the samples and all vOTUS onto an non-metric dimensional scaling
ord_chem<-metaMDS(chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop)
ord_chem # the stress for this should be around <.1

en = envfit(NMDS_Bray_chemistry, chemistry_df_final_input_chemChop, permutations = 999, na.rm = TRUE)

###########Now do the final plot with the loadings as bars.
distance <- function(x, y, home = c(0,0)) {
  sqrt((x-home[1])^2 + (y-home[2])^2)
}

#create loadings df for plot arrows
v_scrs <- as.data.frame(scores(en, display = "vectors"))
v_scrs <- cbind(v_scrs*ordiArrowMul(en), Compound = rownames(v_scrs))

v_scrs <- v_scrs %>%
  mutate(dist_pc1pc2 = distance(NMDS1, NMDS2), #distance in space from center
         scaled_dist = dist_pc1pc2 * 10)

#get top 10 compounds based on distance in space from center
top_dist_compounds <- v_scrs %>%
  arrange(desc(scaled_dist)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  mutate(num_lab = 1:10) %>%
  select(Compound, num_lab)

#make plotting columns for loadings df
v_scrs <- v_scrs %>%
  mutate(top_c = ifelse(Compound %in% top_dist_compounds$Compound,"top","other"),
         alpha_factor = ifelse(top_c == "top", 1, 0.5),
         plot_pc1 = ifelse(top_c == "top", NMDS1, 0),
         plot_pc2 = ifelse(top_c == "top", NMDS2, 0),
         top_label = ifelse(top_c == "top", Compound, "")) %>%
  left_join(top_dist_compounds, by = c("Compound"))

#Now plot on ggplot
library(wesanderson)
library(RColorBrewer)

chem_samplePoint_bars <- data.scores %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2)) +
  geom_segment(data = v_scrs,
               aes(x= 0, xend = NMDS1*20, 
                   y = 0, yend = NMDS2*20, 
                   alpha = alpha_factor,
                   color = Compound),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.5, "cm")),
               inherit.aes = FALSE)  +
  scale_color_manual(values=wes_palette("FantasticFox1", type="continuous", 26)) + 
  geom_text(data = v_scrs,
            aes(label = num_lab,
                x = NMDS1*20,
                y = NMDS2*20),
            size = 3) +
  new_scale_color()+
  geom_point(aes(fill = Sample.Type), size = 4, shape = 21) +
  #stat_ellipse(aes(fill = Sample.Type, color = Sample.Type), alpha = 0.2, geom = "polygon", type="t") +
  theme_bw()
